editorial:
Ever wondered what would happen if you took a centuries-old play and dropped it right into the middle of busy New York City? You get a wild ride where the royal palace becomes a huge corporate empire and the ghost of a dead father shows up on a voicemail machine. You will follow a young man who is totally stressed out and angry because his uncle stole his father's business and married his mother. The vibe is very moody and urban, making the old dialogue feel surprisingly fresh and relatable for someone living in the modern world.

Ethan Hawke does a great job playing a guy who is slowly losing his grip on things. The way the movie uses cameras and city lights makes it feel like a spy movie instead of a boring school project. While the pacing slows down a bit in the middle, the tension builds up perfectly toward the end. You should definitely check this out if you like dramas with a dark edge. To get the best look at the city scenery, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or just rent it on Apple TV for a movie night.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart in a big final fight. Hamlet ends up killing his uncle, Claudius, after discovering he was poisoned. However, it is a sad ending because almost everyone dies. Ophelia is gone, and Hamlet himself is fatally wounded. He spends his last moments making sure the truth about the murder comes out so the world knows what really happened. It wraps up with the corporate empire collapsing and a new leader taking over.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Shakespeare but wants a modern twist.
